problems.device: slip-ring brush assembly of a 1.5 MW generator excitation system running at 1800 rpm
problems.failure: Brush and slip-ring contact wear progresses to arcing and intermittent open-circuit excitation transients weeks before the classical media (vibration, temperature) alarms rise, so operators learn of the failure from the excitation fault itself rather than from a leading indicator.
problems.constraint: the predictor must rely only on data already collected by the plant historian at a 1-minute sampling interval, must fire at least 2 weeks before a forced outage would otherwise occur, and must not raise more than 1 false alarm per year per machine
problems.question: Propose the most cost-effective measurable leading indicator (predictor) for the stated failure, its operating threshold, and the concrete test that would validate or kill the predictor.
user_variables: historian data at 1-minute sampling interval only
at least 2 weeks warning before forced outage
no more than 1 false alarm per year per machine
1800 rpm operating speed

problems.device: subcutaneous insulin pump infusion set with a 90 cm catheter worn by ambulatory type-1 diabetes patients

problems.constraint: raise no more than 1 nuisance occlusion alarm per 14 days of wear, detect a complete occlusion within 15 minutes, and detect partial occlusions (delivery deficit above 20 percent) within 2 hours, without changing the wearable form factor
problems.question: What engineering change, intervention, or design would prevent or mitigate the stated failure under the stated constraint, and what concrete test would falsify the proposed approach?
user_variables: detection of complete occlusion within 15 minutes
partial occlusion (delivery deficit above 20 percent) within 2 hours
no more than 1 nuisance alarm per 14 days of wear
no change to the wearable form factor

problems.device: water-cooled centrifugal chiller condenser tube bank in a district cooling plant using an open cooling tower loop
problems.failure: Condenser tube fouling accumulates silently: the fouling layer raises condenser approach temperature and pressure schedules, but operators clean on a fixed monthly cadence rather than on measured need, so tubes spend part of the month fouled early in the season and the cleaning cadence wastes labor later.
problems.constraint: the predictor must use only BMS points already logged (chilled water supply/return temperature, condenser water supply/return temperature, compressor power, pump speed, outdoor wet-bulb), must resolve fouling state changes within 3 days at full load, and must produce a cleaning trigger that reduces total compressor energy by at least 3 percent versus the fixed monthly cadence
problems.question: Propose the most cost-effective measurable leading indicator (predictor) for the stated failure, its operating threshold, and the concrete test that would validate or kill the predictor.
user_variables: BMS points already logged (listed in constraint)
fouling state resolved within 3 days at full load
at least 3 percent compressor energy reduction vs the fixed monthly cadence
